projects.title: The Marble Kitchen
projects.description: A masterclass in culinary elegance, this kitchen combines book-matched Carrera marble with minimalist charcoal cabinetry to create a space that is as functional as it is beautiful.

narrative.brief: The client sought a culinary sanctuary that echoed the precision of a professional workshop while maintaining the warmth of a social hub.
narrative.vision: We centered the design on a monolithic 4-meter island of book-matched Carrera marble, emphasizing the raw beauty of natural stone patterns.
narrative.execution: Crafted with hidden integrated appliances and bespoke charcoal-stained ash cabinetry, every element was designed to vanish into the architecture.

projects.title: Serene Garden Suite
projects.description: Designed as a retreat from the city, this bedroom features floor-to-ceiling glass walls that invite nature inside, complemented by soft textiles and a muted color palette.

narrative.brief: A request for total immersion in nature without compromising on the security and comfort of a high-end luxury dwelling.
narrative.vision: A glass-box concept where the structure seemingly disappears, blurring the lines between the curated garden and the refined interior.
narrative.execution: Acoustic glazing and hand-woven silk wall coverings ensure that the space remains a silent refuge from the urban pulse of Zurich.

projects.title: The Glass Loft
projects.description: An open-plan living space that celebrates light and volume. High-end furnishings and architectural lines define this modern urban sanctuary.

narrative.brief: The transformation of a former industrial archive into a residence that could double as a private art gallery.
narrative.vision: Maximizing vertical volume through mezzanine levels and utilizing concrete finishes to maintain an industrial soul in a luxury context.
narrative.execution: Polished concrete floors and automated smart-shading systems allow the client to modulate light perfectly for their art collection.

journal.title: The Art of Materiality
journal.excerpt: Exploring the emotional resonance of raw stone and hand-finished timber in modern architecture.
journal.author: Elena Rossi
journal.content:
Materiality isn't just about what a building is made of; it's about how it feels to the touch, how it ages under the sun, and the stories it tells through its grain and texture. In our latest explorations, we've focused on the juxtaposition of cold Carrera marble against the warmth of reclaimed oak.

This dialogue between materials creates a sensory experience that goes beyond the visual. It's about the weight of a stone island in a kitchen, the silent sound of a linen-draped room, and the honesty of exposed steel. We believe that when you strip away the trends, the materials are what remain to anchor a home in reality.
